event.title: perf(UnderlinePanels): eliminate cascading renders on mount and resize
event.body:
Closes #

## Summary

Removes the cascading-render anti-patterns from `UnderlinePanels` —
specifically the one mount-after-effect cycle (props mirrored into state via
`useEffect`), the extra commit from storing `listWidth` in state when nothing
in render reads it, and the tablist-wide reconciliation that happened every
time `iconsVisible` flipped because `cloneElement` baked the flag into every
`Tab` element.

Behavior is identical. The component now renders **once** on mount instead of
twice, never produces an empty-tablist frame, and resize-driven icon toggles
only update each `Tab`'s context-consuming subtree instead of forcing the
whole tablist through reconciliation.

## What was wrong

[`packages/react/src/experimental/UnderlinePanels/UnderlinePanels.tsx`](packages/react/src/experimental/UnderlinePanels/UnderlinePanels.tsx) on `main`
had three independent sources of unnecessary renders:

### 1. Props mirrored in state via `useEffect`

```tsx
const [tabs, setTabs] = useState<React.ReactNode[]>([])
const [tabPanels, setTabPanels] = useState<React.ReactNode[]>([])

useEffect(() => {
  // clone children → newTabs / newTabPanels
  setTabs(newTabs)
  setTabPanels(newTabPanels)
}, [children, parentId, loadingCounters, iconsVisible])
```

The React docs flag this exact pattern as an anti-pattern. Mount sequence:

- Render 1: `tabs = []`, `tabPanels = []` → renders an empty tablist for one frame.
- Effect runs → two `setState`s (batched into one commit).
- Render 2: actual tabs appear.

Every prop change re-ran the effect → another setState → another commit.

### 2. `listWidth` stored in state but only read inside the resize callback

```tsx
const [listWidth, setListWidth] = useState(0)
useIsomorphicLayoutEffect(() => {
  setListWidth(listRef.current?.getBoundingClientRect().width ?? 0)
}, [tabsHaveIcons])

useResizeObserver(([entry]) => {
  setIconsVisible(entry.contentRect.width > listWidth)
}, wrapperRef, [])
```

Render never reads `listWidth`. The state existed solely to be read inside
the resize-observer callback. Each write was a wasted commit.

### 3. `iconsVisible` and `loadingCounters` baked into every Tab via `cloneElement`

```tsx
return cloneElement(child, {id: `${parentId}-tab-${tabIndex++}`, loadingCounters, iconsVisible})
```

Both flags were in the effect's deps array, so the moment `iconsVisible`
flipped (from the resize observer), the effect re-ran, every Tab element was
re-cloned with new props, and React reconciled fresh Tab elements across the
entire tablist. A consumer with 12 tabs would see all 12 Tab function bodies
re-execute on every resize that crossed the icon-fits threshold.

## What this PR does

Four commits, each independently shippable and tests-green:

### [`perf(UnderlinePanels): derive tabs and panels in render, not from state`](https://github.com/primer/react/pull/<id>/commits/2556ac453)

Replaces the `useState` + `useEffect` pair with a single `useMemo` that walks
`children`, clones tabs/panels with their IDs, and returns the partitioned
arrays. The empty-tablist mount frame is gone; consumer rerenders no longer
do the two-commit dance.

### [`perf(UnderlinePanels): keep list width in a ref, not state`](https://github.com/primer/react/pull/<id>/commits/b8e01f64c)

`listWidth` moves from `useState` to `useRef`. The layout effect writes
`ref.current`; the resize-observer callback reads `ref.current`. The only
state setter left in the resize path is `setIconsVisible`, which only fires
when the decision actually flips.

### [`perf(UnderlinePanels): pass iconsVisible / loadingCounters via context`](https://github.com/primer/react/pull/<id>/commits/9c33899a9)

Introduces a new internal `UnderlinePanelsContext` carrying `iconsVisible`
and `loadingCounters`. The `cloneElement` call now only assigns the
generated `id`, and the memo deps drop to `[children, parentId]`. Tabs read
the flags from context, so they still react to resize-driven toggles —
context propagation does the work, not element re-cloning.

`React.memo(Tab)` ties the bow: with referentially-stable Tab elements +
memo, an `iconsVisible` flip updates only each Tab's context-consuming
subtree, not the surrounding tablist.

### [`test(UnderlinePanels): pin no-empty-frame, bounded mount renders, memo stability`](https://github.com/primer/react/pull/<id>/commits/f8deeaa5f)

Three new tests that pin every claim above:

1. **`renders tabs synchronously on mount (no empty-tablist frame)`** — runs
   `render(...)`, queries `[role="tab"]` immediately, expects 3 tabs. If a
   future change reintroduces state-from-effect, the count is 0 on render
   return and this trips.
2. **`bounds parent renders on initial mount`** — wraps `UnderlinePanels`
   in a render-counted host and asserts the host renders ≤ 1 time on mount.
3. **`does not re-render tabs when an unrelated re-render of the parent occurs`** —
   renders a stable `tree` reference, triggers three unrelated parent
   re-renders via `rerender(...)`, asserts the TabBody count inside Tabs
   stays at its mount-time value. Catches any future change that re-bakes
   `iconsVisible` / `loadingCounters` into Tab via cloneElement or drops the
   `React.memo` wrapper.

Plus a patch changeset.

## Profiles

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Mount renders of UnderlinePanels | 2 (initial + effect-setState) | 1 |
| Empty-tablist frame on mount | yes (1 frame) | no |
| `listWidth` setState | per mount + per list-width change | gone |
| Tab re-renders on `iconsVisible` flip | every Tab, every flip | only context consumers; surrounding subtree untouched |
| Cascade through unrelated parent re-renders | yes (Tab elements re-cloned) | no (memo + context) |

### Changelog

#### New

- Internal `UnderlinePanelsContext` carrying `iconsVisible` and
  `loadingCounters` for the Tab component.

#### Changed

- `UnderlinePanels` derives tabs/panels in render (`useMemo`) instead of
  syncing props into state via `useEffect`.
- `UnderlinePanels.Tab` is wrapped in `React.memo` and reads
  `iconsVisible` / `loadingCounters` from context instead of via
  `cloneElement`-injected props.
- `listWidth` is kept in a ref instead of state.

#### Removed

- The mount-time empty-tablist frame.
- The `setListWidth` state setter (its value lives in a ref now).

### Rollout strategy

- [x] Patch release
- [ ] Minor release
- [ ] Major release; if selected, include a written rollout or migration plan
- [ ] None; if selected, include a brief description as to why

`UnderlinePanels` is `experimental`. Public API is unchanged; consumers get
the perf win automatically.

### Testing & Reviewing

```bash
cd packages/react
npx vitest run --project '@primer/react (chromium)' src/experimental/UnderlinePanels/UnderlinePanels.test.tsx
# 14 tests pass (11 pre-existing + 3 new perf-regression pins)
```

**Reviewer focus:**

1. The `useMemo` deps are `[children, parentId]` — `iconsVisible` and
   `loadingCounters` are no longer in there. Verify this is correct: those
   flags reach Tab via context, so the memo doesn't need to invalidate when
   they change.
2. The `React.memo(Tab)` cast: `Tab.__SLOT__` and `Tab.displayName` are
   still set correctly on the memo wrapper so `isSlot(child, Tab)` and
   `child.type === Tab` keep working through cloneElement.
3. The third regression test (`does not re-render tabs when an unrelated
   re-render of the parent occurs`) relies on Tab having referentially
   stable React element identity across the host's `rerender(...)` —
   verify the `tree` constant pattern in the test models real consumer
   usage.

### Merge checklist

- [x] Added/updated tests
- [x] Added/updated documentation (changeset)
- [ ] Added/updated previews (Storybook)
- [x] Changes are [SSR compatible](https://github.com/primer/react/blob/main/contributor-docs/CONTRIBUTING.md#ssr-compatibility)
- [x] Tested in Chrome
- [ ] Tested in Firefox
- [ ] Tested in Safari
- [ ] Tested in Edge
- [ ] (GitHub staff only) Integration tests pass at github/github-ui ([Learn more about how to run integration tests](https://github.com/github/primer-engineering/blob/main/how-we-work/testing-primer-react-pr-at-dotcom.md))
